Name:  ___                Unit No:   ___
 
Admission Date:  ___              Discharge Date:   ___
 
Date of Birth:  ___             Sex:   M
 
Service: MEDICINE
 
Allergies: 
Gluten / Augmentin
 
Attending: ___.
 
Chief Complaint:
Abdominal pain, fever
 
Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure:
ERCP with sphincterotomy and stent placement
 
History of Present Illness:
Mr. ___ is an ___ year old man with history of refractory 
celiac disease, hypertension, history of pulmonary embolism, 
cystic pancreatic lesions, and osteoporosis who presents after 
an episode of acute abdominal pain. The pain started at 8:30pm 
the night prior to admission, and he describes it as a sharp 
pain of acute onset radiating from the abdomen to the back, 
rated ___. It was associated with nausea and two episodes of 
vomiting. He reports eating a dinner of scrambled eggs and 
peppers and a blueberry muffin for dinner the night prior. He 
had three bowel movements, which were normal. He called his 
primary care doctor, and the coverage referred him to the ED for 
further evaluation. He subsequently called EMS and was 
transferred to an OSH.  
.
Per his report, he was given IV morphine with some improvement 
in the pain at the OSH. He was then transferred to ___. In our 
ED, he was initially scheduled for ___ and CT torso (which he 
declined), given concern for possible DVT/PE. His transaminases 
were elevated (AST 124, ALT 90, alk phos 218, tbili 2.0) and 
lipase was elevated at 781. He then had an ultrasound which 
showed multiple gallstones without evidence of cholecystitis. He 
was noted to be febrile to Tmax 101.3. He was given a dose of IV 
levofloxacin and IV metronidazole, as well as three liters of 
IVF, and transferred to the floor for further evaluation. 
.
Of note, he recently had a CT scan of his abdomen which showed a 
pancreatic cyst, unchanged from previous. He was told that 
nothing more needed to be done; however, the final read also 
mentions that the appearance of the pancreatic head and uncinate 
process appears to have changed with an exophytic area 
projecting from the posterior aspect of the uncinate process, 
possibly corresponding to an exophytic dilated pancreatic side 
branch/cyst versus a lymph node immediately adjacent to the 
pancreas. There is no mention of this in the notes. 
.
Review of systems: He reports left lower extremity swelling (and 
recent cellulitis, treated with Keflex). He denies feeling 
febrile, chills, weight loss, 
 
Past Medical History:
- Refractory Celiac Disease; currently getting TPN four nights a 
week, followed by Dr. ___
- ___ hypertension 
- Iron deficiency anemia 
- RLL pulmonary embolism - incidental finding after a CT scan 
was performed for evaluation of possible pancreatic mass. On 
coumadin x six to seven months, stopped recently.  
- Cystic Pancreatic Lesions - followed with serial CT scans  
- Kidney Stone - work up of this showed possible pancreatic mass 
 
- Anxiety disorder  
- Subclinical hypothyroidism  
- Peripheral neuropathy  
- Osteoporosis - not on a bisphosphonate  
- Hypogonadism  

 
Social History:
___

No other family members known to have celiac sprue although he 
thinks several people who died at a young age may have had it.

appearing.

Abd: Tender to deep palpation, particularly around umbilicus. No

RUQ ultrasound ___ IMPRESSION: 
1. Cholelithiasis without evidence of acute cholecystitis. 
2. Multiple hyperechoic areas in the left lobe of the liver, 
could not be 
well evaluated in this study. Recommended a repeat ultrasound or 
a CT of the abdomen with contrast (favored) for further 
evaluation. 
.
ERCP ___
 Cannulation of the biliary duct was successful and deep with a 
sphincterotome using a free-hand technique. 
The common bile duct, common hepatic duct, right and left 
hepatic ducts, biliary radicles, cystic duct, and gallbladder 
were filled with contrast and well visualized. 
There was a filling defect at the distal ___ of the CBD. This 
was consistent with a small stone or sludge. 
There was an irregularity of the CBD consistent with possible 
cholangitis. 
The gallbladder had multiple filling defects consistent with 
stones.   
A small biliary sphincterotomy was performed in the 12 o'clock 
position using a sphincterotome over an existing guidewire.  
A ___ by 9cm biliary stent was placed successfully using a 
Oasis ___ stent introducer kit.  
Recommendations: If any problems- please call Dr. ___ at 
___.
No aspirin, plavix, NSAIDS, coumadin for 72 hours.
Follow for response and complications. If any abdominal pain, 
fever, jaundice, gastrointestinal bleeding please call ERCP 
fellow on call (___)
NPO for now. Re-assess in ___ hours, if does well and has gag 
reflex start clears.
Repeat ERCP in ___ weeks for stent removal, balloon sweep and 
pancreatic duct evaluation. Pancreatogram was not done today as 
pt was septic. 
Vitamin K subcutaneously tonight- check INR in AM. 
Will eventually require surgical evaluation for cholecystectomy. 

.
RUQ U/S ___ COMPARISON: Multiple abdominal ultrasounds, most 
recent of ___. FINDINGS: The liver demonstrates 
normal echotexture throughout without focal lesions seen. The 
main portal vein is patent with appropriate direction of flow. 
There is no intra- or extra-hepatic biliary dilatation. The 
gallbladder again contains multiple stones. However, there are 
no secondary signs of cholecystitis. The patient had a negative 
sonographic ___ sign. IMPRESSION: Cholelithiasis without 
evidence of cholecystitis. No significant change since prior 
study.  
.
___ CTA chest
REASON FOR EXAM: Dyspnea, leukocytosis, cough. Exclude PE, 
pneumonia. 
TECHNIQUE: MDCT axial images of the chest were obtained at full 
expiration 
using low-dose technique without contrast followed by a 
full-dose technique at full inspiration after a rapid bolus of 
100 mL of IV Optiray contrast with multiplanar reformats. 
FINDINGS: There is satisfactory contrast opacification to the 
segmental level bilaterally. No pulmonary embolism, aortic 
dissection or aneurysm. 
The thoracic esophagus is patulous throughout its course with a 
small hiatal hernia. Airways are widely patent to subsegmental 
level bilaterally. No pathologic enlargement of the mediastinal 
or axillary lymph nodes by CT size criteria. The aorta and 
pulmonary artery are normal. Heart size is top normal with a 
minimal pericardial effusion which is most likely physiological. 
Calcification in the coronary arteries is moderate with mild 
calcification of the aortic valve.   
Moderately large bilateral pleural effusions are noted with 
focal ground-glass opacity in the right upper lobe (4:17 and 
4:20) which could be due to resolving pulmonary edema or 
possibly recent infection or inflammation. 
Limited views of the upper abdomen reveals a biliary stent with 
pneumobilia. Multiple wedge compression fractures of the mid and 
lower thoracic spine are of uncertain chronicity probably 
longstanding 
IMPRESSION: 1)No pulmonary embolism, aortic dissection or 
aneurysm.   
2)Moderately large bilateral pleural effusions with multifocal 
ground-glass opacities in the right upper lobe could be due to 
resolving pulmonary edema or infection. 3)Multilevel 
degenerative changes in the thoracic spine with wedge 
compression fractures of indeterminate chronicity. 4)Biliary 
stent with pneumobilia. 
.

 
Brief Hospital Course:
___ with history of celiac disease, hypertension, osteoporosis, 
and prior pulmonary embolism admitted with episode of abdominal 
pain, fever, due to cholestasis and gallstone pancreatitis; 
course complicated by Pneumonia, bilateral pleural 
effusions/volume overload and new onset atrial fibrillation.  
.
#) Fever. Most concerning source is biliary (i.e. cholangitis) 
given abdominal pain, cholestasis, and fever. A blood culture 
from admission demonstrated gram negative rods; he was initially 
placed on cefepime and then transitioned to Unasyn and flagyl 
___ when the culture grew pan-sensitive E. coli.  This was 
changed to ceftriaxone/azithromycin on ___ for PNA as below.  
.
#) Abdominal pain. S/p ERCP ___, small stone/sludge 
extraction, stent placement. Surgery was consulted; based on 
repeat imaging, labs and exam did not feel urgent intervention 
was required.  The patient should follow up with Dr ___ 
the surgeon of his choosing for an elective out patient 
cholecystectomy in ___ months. He will need a repeat ERCP in ___ 
weeks for stent removal, balloon sweep and pancreatic duct 
evaluation. 
***He will require serial LFTs to ensure stability while at 
rehab. Discharge LFTS: ALT 47 AST 37 AlkPhos 212 TotBili 1.4.  

#) Leukocytosis/Cough: Pneumonia.  On ___ his WBC increased to 
18, then trended up to 26.9 on ___.  ERCP and Surgery did not 
feel it was a GI/gallbladder source.  Repeat ultrasound without 
significant change, surgery re-consulted (continue to be 
unconcerned).  CTA was performed; negative for PE but notable 
for RUL opacities concerning for infection as well as moderate 
bilateral effusions (thought due to volume overload in setting 
of volume resuscitation on presentation with septic physiology). 
 He was started on a ceftriaxone / azithromycin on ___ with 
improvement of cough and leukocytosis; he will complete 10 days 
of abx.   He was diuresed with IV lasix on ___ and ___. 
***He will require serial CBCs at rehab to ensure continued 
normalization of his White count: CBC on discharge: White Blood 
Cells 18.4*; Hemoglobin 8.2, Platelets 434.  
--He will also require management of his volume status and Lasix 
PRN for his pulmonary effusions (presumed volume overload).  
--He will require a repeat pa and lateral CXR in 1 week to 
reassess his pneumonia and pleural effusions. 
.
#) Atrial fibrillation. Developed new onset atrial fibrillation 
in the setting of bacteremia/high fevers. TSH normal ___. His 
last TTE (___) showed only mild left atrial enlargement. He has 
been on coumadin in the past (for DVT/PE), he is not interested 
in restarting this medication (he has ongoing vitamin K 
deficiency and it is very difficult for him to be therapeutic on 
coumadin). TTE cardioversion was discussed with the patient, but 
he declined the necessary anticoagulation for one month 
following the procedure. Lovenox was also discussed; he was not 
interested. He is aware of the increased stroke risk of 
untreated afib (CHADS2 =2).  His baby aspirin was increased to a 
full 325 mg daily.  He was rate controlled with his home regimen 
of metoprolol. He will follow up with his PCP for further 
evaluation/management. 
.
# Anemia: The patient has a chronic anemia with baseline 
Hemoglobin ranging from ___. His Hemoglobin at discharge was 
8.2.  Continues on B12 and folate. 
***He will require periodic CBC to monitor hematocrit and ensure 
it remains within this range. 

#) CT findings from ___: "Appearance of the pancreatic head 
and uncinate process appears to have changed with an exophytic 
area projecting from the posterior aspect of the uncinate 
process, possibly corresponding to an exophytic dilated 
pancreatic 
side branch/cyst versus a lymph node immediately adjacent to the 
pancreas. Clarification with MRCP is recommended."  Management 
as per Dr ___ may be readdressed at the time of his repeat 
ERCP in ___ weeks. Left lobe of liver hypoechoic lesions seen on 
ultrasound are likely same lesion seen on CT from ___: 6 mm 
in diameter in segment II of the liver most likely representing 
a simple cyst and unchanged compared to prior study.
.
#) Celiac disease. The patient was continued on TPN; tis was 
given daily in house in the setting of increased metabolic 
demands with acute illness; he should transition back to 4 
nights/week when he goes home from rehab.  He will follow up 
with Dr. ___ as an outpatient. **All oral medications MUST 
be verified at gluten free.**  
.
#) Hypertension. Continue BP meds, with strict holding 
parameters.

You were admitted with abdominal pain due to gallstones.  An
